STEP 0 — DEEP RESEARCH FIRST (DO THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE — MANDATORY)
Before writing a single word of narration or any image prompt, thoroughly RESEARCH the given Topic and Source Material. Do not skip this. A shallow script produces a failed video.

Research silently and establish:

Verified core facts — what actually happened, who was involved, where and when. Separate confirmed fact from legend, regional retelling, and popular myth.

The single strongest HOOK ANGLE — the most surprising, emotional, or high-stakes entry point a cold viewer would stop scrolling for.

The core EMOTION of this episode (one word) and the single PAYOFF the viewer gets at the end.

Visual opportunities — which 3–5 moments are inherently cinematic and what each looks like (era, location, costume, light, scale).

Uncertainties — anything sources disagree on or you cannot verify. NEVER invent quotations, Sanskrit verses, dates, statistics, dialogue from scripture, or miracles presented as scientific proof. Omit unsupported specifics or qualify them briefly.

Only after this research is solid, proceed to the workflow below. Source fidelity over invention — but emotion and clarity over dry recitation.

🕉️ RAMAYANA — ADI KAVYA
MASTER PROMPT FILE (Merged) — Version 7.3 IMAGE-ONLY
Bible + Script Prompt + Image-Only Production Prompt + Workflow Guide, in one document — Static Visual Edition
This single file merges the original documents into one complete IMAGE-ONLY visual production system with Studio Motion Graphics.

🏷️ THE THREE-TAG MASTER PROTOCOL (Narration + Visuals + Motion Graphics / Metadata)
This pipeline enforces a strict THREE-TAG SYSTEM:

1. Audio Narration Tag: Exactly one <script>...</script> block housing the clean TTS-ready narration in Section 2B. Spoken Devanagari Hindi only.

2. Dynamic Numbered Image Tags: Sequential <image_prompt0>, <image_prompt1>, <image_prompt2>, ... <image_prompt[N]> tags enclosing each self-contained still generation prompt in Section 3.
- Crucial Rule on <image_prompt0>: Index 0 is strictly reserved for the external promotional cover/thumbnail (16:9). It is never placed inside the video editing timeline.
- Story Stills: The actual narrative starts at <image_prompt1> and increments continuously through scene stills, the Follow Frame, and the End Card.

3. Dynamic Motion Graphics & Metadata Tags: Sequential <metadata1>, <metadata2>, ... <metadata[N]> tags specifying high-retention studio motion graphics (scripture scrolls, era timelines, sacred maps, relic reticles, canto titles).
The AI decides where and when to trigger each motion graphic based on the sacred story beats, but MUST include them where relevant:

Available Motion Graphic Archetypes for <metadata>:
- scripture_scroll: Use for sacred Sanskrit shlokas, ancient verses, or prophetic decrees with Hindi meaning/translation. Displays authentic aged parchment/copper-plate card with golden callout.
  Format:
  <metadata1>
  #scene 2
  Type: scripture_scroll
  Title: [Sanskrit Shloka / Key Mantra]
  Detail: [Source e.g. VALMIKI RAMAYANA // BALA KANDA or Translation]
  </metadata1>

- telemetry_counter: Use whenever explicit numbers, years of exile/penance, elapsed centuries, arrow counts, or astronomical alignments are spoken. Displays rapid odometer ticker count up (0 -> target).
  Format:
  <metadata2>
  #scene 4
  Type: telemetry_counter
  Target: [Integer numeral e.g. 14]
  Unit: [YEARS / BCE / YUGA / ARROWS]
  Label: [ERA / PENANCE / DURATION]
  Detail: [Context e.g. 14 Years of Forest Exile]
  </metadata2>

- route_map: Use for epic journeys, exile paths, flight routes (Pushpaka Vimana), or sacred trails (Ayodhya -> Dandaka -> Kishkindha -> Lanka). Displays animated vector route line drawing with radar destination ping.
  Format:
  <metadata3>
  #scene 6
  Type: route_map
  Origin: [Starting location e.g. Ayodhya]
  Destination: [Arrival place e.g. Panchavati]
  Distance: [Route descriptor e.g. DANDAKARANYA TRAIL]
  Detail: [Sacred Exile Journey]
  </metadata3>

- relic_spotlight: Use to direct viewer focus to a sacred divine weapon (Sharanga Bow, Brahmastra), holy relic (Chudamani, Rama's signet ring), or temple architecture visible in the scene. Displays pulsing targeting reticle and callout line.
  Format:
  <metadata4>
  #scene 8
  Type: object_spotlight
  Target: [Sacred item visible in scene e.g. Kodanda Bow / Sanjeevani Herb]
  Title: [Name of Sacred Relic / Astra]
  Detail: [Divine power / Origin / Significance]
  </metadata4>

- polaroid_badge: Use when introducing a legendary sage, king, avatar, or warrior (e.g. Maharishi Vishwamitra, Jatayu, Meghanada). Displays card cutout with 3D tilt and drifting motion over the scene. Must include an Asset Prompt for an isolated subject on clean background.
  Format:
  <metadata5>
  #scene 3
  Type: polaroid_badge
  Title: [Character Name e.g. MAHARISHI VISHWAMITRA]
  Detail: [Lineage / Title / Role e.g. Brahmarshi / Preceptor]
  Asset Prompt: [Self-contained visual prompt for isolated subject on clean background]
  </metadata5>

- chapter_title: Use for major canto openings, act breaks, or epic turning points. Bold cinematic typography with accent tag.
  Format:
  <metadata6>
  #scene 1
  Type: chapter_title
  Title: [Canto / Chapter Headline e.g. THE LEAP TO LANKA]
  Tag: [BALA KANDA / ARANYA KANDA / SUNDARA KANDA]
  </metadata6>

PART 3 — 🕉️ SCRIPT PROMPT (Creative Pass — Run FIRST)
Take raw content and output a locked Hindi script. Never generate images or visual prompts in this pass.

Content Setup & Rules
Hook Rule: The first 3–6 spoken words must begin a concrete, source-supported action, dilemma or contrast with immediate emotional stakes. Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.

Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. Follow the 5–8 word turn with its concrete explanation; do not merely announce that a twist is coming. Preserve devotional dignity and source fidelity. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.

Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.

Ending: Story reaches completion first; followed by ONE single closing blessing line of at most 3 seconds. Resolve the opening promise with the actual outcome and the decisive reason, action or cost before any closing line. Place the strongest earned payoff in the final story beat, with useful smaller payoffs beforehand; never stretch an already answered question or hide a known outcome behind fake mystery. Finish on a concise consequence or an earlier detail whose meaning has changed, without recapping the story or adding a generic moral. A callback may reward replay only after the story is complete; no forced cliffhanger or missing answer. Preserve the existing CTA or blessing requirement and keep it brief, after resolution; add no extra engagement requests. No "wait until the end," "you won't believe," or empty "but then everything changed" lines.

# Research Dossier: The Acoustic Mystery of Airavathesvara Temple (12th-Century Chola Singing Stone Steps)

---

## 1. Verified Facts, Background & Key Data
* **Location & Site Status:** Located in Darasuram (near Kumbakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu, India). It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and part of the "Great Living Chola Temples" trio (along with Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur and Gangaikondacholapuram).
* **Historical Chronology:** Built during the 12th century CE (circa 1146–1163 CE / completed around 1166 CE) by the Chola Emperor **Rajaraja Chola II**.
* **The Architectural Phenomenon:** Near the *Balipeetham* or the entrance porch of the *Agra Mandapa* (the front hall designed in the shape of a chariot), there is a short, ornately carved flight of steps traditionally referred to as the **Singing Steps** (*Saptha Swara Padalgal*).
* **Acoustic / Lithophonic Reality:** When struck or stepped upon with precise distribution, these granite steps emit distinct tones corresponding to the 7 classical Carnatic musical notes (*Swaras*: Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni). 
* **Engineering Science:** This is a classic example of ancient **lithophonic architecture**. The acoustic resonance is achieved through precise manipulation of stone geometry (length, width, thickness, mass, hollow air columns/undercuts beneath or inside the block, and the density of hard igneous granite/charnockite stone) rather than modern electronics or metal parts.
* **Preservation Status:** Due to modern tourist vandalism and unmindful striking with heavy objects, the musical stairs are currently covered with protective metal mesh/grids by authorities.

---

## 2. Chronological Story Arc & Scene Beats (~90s)

* **Hook (0:00 - 0:12) [The Mystery]:** 
  * *Visual:* Close-up macro shot of carved Chola granite stone steps under warm amber temple light, with a foot lightly stepping down, triggering invisible musical waves [Viewer promise established].

* **Setup & Traditional Lore (0:12 - 0:35) [Context]:**
  * *Visual:* Cinematic pull-back showing the 12th-century chariot-shaped *Agra Mandapa* of the Airavathesvara Temple in Darasuram, built by Rajaraja Chola II.
  * *Narration:* Tamil Nadu के द्वारासुरम में स्थित यह यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल, ऐरावतेश्वर मंदिर, चोल वास्तुकला का एक अद्भुत चमत्कार है। यहाँ मंदिर के प्रवेश द्वार पर बनी सात सीढ़ियाँ साधारण नहीं हैं।
* **Escalation & Scientific Reveal (0:35 - 1:05) [Engineering Explanation]:**
  * *Visual:* Detailed close-up panning across the granite steps, showing intricate stone craftsmanship, highlighting how geometry and material density create sound.
  * *Narration:* इन्हें 'संगीत सीढ़ियाँ' कहा जाता है। जब इन्हें बजाया जाता है, तो इनसे भारतीय शास्त्रीय संगीत के सातों स्वर (स, री, ग, म...) गूंजते हैं। यह कोई जादू नहीं, बल्कि प्राचीन शिल्पशास्त्र और चोल स्थापत्य की उत्कृष्ट ध्वनिकी (Acoustics) है।
* **Climax & Payoff (1:05 - 1:20) [The Lithophonic Fact]:**
  * *Visual:* Close-up texture shot of hard granite stone edge glowing in golden hour sunlight, emphasizing pure stone engineering without metal or electronics.
  * *Narration:* चोल शिल्पकारों ने ग्रेनाइट पत्थरों की मोटाई, लंबाई और उनके नीचे के वायु अंतरालों (Air Columns) को इस गणितीय सटीकता से तराशा कि बिना किसी यंत्र के पत्थर खुद संगीत पैदा करने लगे।
* **Resolution & Reflection CTA (1:20 - 1:30) [Meaningful Insight]:**
  * *Visual:* Wide angle of the majestic temple vimana silhouetted against a golden dusk sky, fading to a clean end card.
  * *Narration:* यह इस बात का प्रमाण है कि हमारे पूर्वजों के लिए विज्ञान और कला दो अलग रास्ते नहीं, बल्कि एक ही ब्रह्मांडीय लय का हिस्सा थे। क्या आपने कभी ऐसे किसी वास्तुकला के चमत्कार को देखा है? हमें कमेंट में बताएं।

---

## 3. Visual & World-Building Canon
* **Setting & Era:** 12th-century Chola Empire (Darasuram, Tamil Nadu). Intricately sculpted Dravidian stone architecture.
* **Lighting & Atmosphere:** Warm amber sunrise/sunset golden hour lighting (`golden hour lighting`, `warm side-light`), highlighting deep stone reliefs, textures, and chiseled edges without any modern elements.

* **Color Palette:** Rich earthy tones, deep granite greys, amber gold highlights, and terracotta accents.

---

## 4. Scriptwriter Directives
* **Spoken Language:** Hindi / Hinglish (Devanagari script for narration lines). Keep the tone respectful, awe-inspiring, and scientifically grounded.
* **Mandatory Factual Anchors to Include:** 
  * 12th Century / Rajaraja Chola II / Darasuram, Tamil Nadu.

Complete a clear opening thought within the first 1–3 seconds; name the relevant person or sacred object instead of a vague "this" or "he". Let the unanswered question arise from why the action matters, not from hiding who is involved. No channel greetings, series titles, background lecture or invented sacred dialogue. Keep the central question clear while giving an early concrete answer, clue or consequence in the next one or two sentences. Every following sentence must change what the viewer knows, what the protagonist can do, or what the choice will cost. Connect beats through cause and effect; cut repeated setup, biography before the predicament, redundant adjectives and generic suspense. Aim for a meaningful development about every 5–8 seconds where the story supports it, inside the existing scene structure; this is a writing guide, not a cut, scene-count or speech-speed requirement. Use short, natural spoken sentences, clear subjects and concrete verbs. Never hide basic context just to manufacture curiosity. Silently compare three different opening lines and use the clearest, most specific one that the story actually pays off; output only the chosen line in the existing format. Read the opening without the title: the viewer must understand the situation and have a specific reason to hear the next sentence. Remove any line that adds neither necessary context nor a new development. These are editorial choices, not guaranteed audience metrics.Midpoint Re-Hook: At 50–60% mark, use a concise source-supported discovery, decision or consequence that changes the meaning of an earlier detail or raises the cost of the next action. A smaller resolved question should lead naturally into the remaining central question.Language: Simple, poignant, spoken Devanagari Hindi with temple-katha resonance.Ending: Story reaches completion first; followed by ONE single closing blessing line of at most 3 seconds. Resolve the opening promise with the actual outcome and the decisive reason, action or cost before any closing line. Place the strongest earned payoff in the final story beat, with useful smaller payoffs beforehand; never stretch an already answered question or hide a known outcome behind fake mystery. Finish on a concise consequence or an earlier detail whose meaning has changed, without recapping the story or adding a generic moral. A callback may reward replay only after the story is complete; no forced cliffhanger or missing answer. Preserve the existing CTA or blessing requirement and keep it brief, after resolution; add no extra engagement requests.
